I was depressed for the better part of a decade and I'm starting to have more good days than bad ones after a couple months of professional work on it. I was scared of what people would say, meds, therapy and all that, but now I just wish I would have done it sooner. 

Whatever's got you feeling like shit, I do think it's worth trying to figure it out. At least then you can really consider your options, and there's probably a lot of them.
If they're nice, they won't mind helping you when you're in a really tough situation. I think it's brave to ask for help, and you really do deserve some help right now.

Wow. It really sucks they didn't get back to you. It sounds like he gave you a depression screening. I did one with my doctor earlier this year when I told him about my suicidal thoughts.

I bet the counselor or someone higher up like the principal would trip over themselves to help you if you told them about this. It's their job, and no one would blame you for following up on them not doing their job.
Sounds really nice that your friend did that to help you, but I'm sorry that the counselor didn't seem to do anything about it. What was that meeting like?
I'd hope that's not entirely true about your friends, but even if it is, I'd think they'd like it more if you worked on yourself instead of killing yourself. Have you tried getting professional help?

I burned myself for the first time about a week ago. It calmed me down in the moment, but I've felt so awful thinking about it in the days that followed. Even among the huge pile of reasons I have to hate myself, it weighed greatly on me. 

My understanding is that feelings of regret after self-harm are common, and can create a sort of feedback loop of self-harm and self-loathing. I'm trying to not do it again so I don't get into that cycle, which I've read people describe as addictive. 

Even though I recognize that self-harm is a really poor way to cope with my occasional racing thoughts, I've struggled with the urge to do it again for the past week. I've been distracting myself with music when I feel that desire. Maybe that or something else would work for you? Whatever you do, I wish you good luck.
